name: jm-chambers
description: Pairs with flows/jm-chambers.json. Tests a REFUSAL, which inverts the usual logic: here the interstitial APPEARING is the pass, and a run that sailed through to a Full Trial would mean the gate is not holding. Everything downstream depends on that one moment, so it is the guard.

items.claim: A Full Trial was actually requested (not a Quick Ruling by accident)
items.falsifiedBy: no `full trial requested` chapter — the form submitted something else and the gate was never asked the question

items.claim: GUARD — the bench refused and offered chambers instead
items.falsifiedBy: no `chambers offered` chapter. Either the gate let a second Full Trial through (the ledger is not holding) or the refusal arrived too slowly to have preceded the spend, which is the entire point of the downgrade

items.claim: The downgrade was OFFERED, not applied silently — the user had to accept it
items.falsifiedBy: no `chambers accepted` chapter, i.e. a ruling appeared without anyone choosing it. A submit that quietly ran something smaller than what was asked for is a worse betrayal than the paywall it replaced

items.claim: The chambers hearing actually produced a ruling
items.falsifiedBy: no `chambers ruling landed` chapter — the consolation prize does not exist, which is worse than refusing outright

items.claim: No uncaught exceptions or unhandled rejections on the refusal path
items.falsifiedBy: any page error — this path has never run before, so it is the likeliest place for one

items.claim: No console errors on the refusal path
items.falsifiedBy: any console error. A 402 handled correctly should NOT surface as a console error; if it does, the client is treating a designed refusal as a fault

items.claim: No request failed except, possibly, the DESIGNED 402 on the trial route
items.falsifiedBy: any 4xx/5xx that is not a 402. The 402 is the gate working; anything else on this path is the gate breaking. Whether a 402 appears at all depends on which layer caught it first — the client pre-flight refuses before the request is made, so its ABSENCE here is not evidence the server gate is missing

items.claim: The chambers ruling is COMPLETE — not the 3-finding truncation the old paywall gave
items.falsifiedBy: a findings list capped at 3 with an unlock teaser. That would reproduce the exact failure the downgrade replaced, one tier down and invisibly

items.claim: The stored record carries paywallExempt:true — the mechanism fired, not merely the appearance of completeness
items.falsifiedBy: the field absent on the persisted review. Completeness could then be an accident of the daily counter rather than the exemption, and would break the day the counter moved

items.claim: The refusal stays in the cave — courtroom register, never 'quota exceeded' or 'upgrade to Pro'
items.falsifiedBy: any SaaS-register copy on the interstitial. Product #6C: every seam the user meets is in-world or the theatre cracks
